### Rounders (1998) — Risk, Loyalty & The High-Stakes World of Poker ♠️

Rounders is a crime drama starring Matt Damon as Mike McDermott, a talented poker player who dreams of making it big through his skills at the table. After losing a large amount of money in a high-stakes game, Mike decides to leave gambling behind and focus on building a more stable future. But when his childhood friend Worm, played by Edward Norton, returns with dangerous debts, Mike is pulled back into the underground poker world.

As the pressure builds, Mike must navigate ruthless opponents, dangerous loan sharks, and games where one wrong decision can cost him everything. Torn between his ambition and loyalty to his friend, he risks his future to help Worm escape his financial troubles. Every hand becomes a test of patience, strategy, and the ability to read people before they make their move.

The film explores risk, friendship, ambition, discipline, and the consequences of poor decisions. It shows that success requires more than luck; it demands emotional control, careful observation, and the courage to walk away when the odds are against you.

What makes Rounders memorable is its intense portrayal of underground poker and the psychology behind every bet. Beneath the money and competition lies a deeper struggle between chasing a dream and protecting the life you've worked hard to build.

💬 “In a game where everyone has a plan, the real advantage belongs to the one who knows when to fold.”

source_details.synopsis: Rounders is a 1998 American crime drama film about the underground world of high-stakes poker, directed by John Dahl and starring Matt Damon and Edward Norton. The story follows two friends who need to win at high-stakes poker to quickly pay off a large debt. The term "rounder" refers to a person traveling around from city to city seeking high-stakes card games. Rounders premiered at the Venice Film Festival on September 4, 1998, and was theatrically released in the United States on September 11.
